standard_prerequisites.name: On an affine scheme the derived category of quasi-coherent modules compares with the derived category of modules, perfect objects correspond to bounded complexes of finite projective modules, and the tensor product of derived quasi-coherent objects is represented by the total complex of the tensor product double complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Translates the affine case into countability of cohomology of module complexes.

core_obligations: Reduce Ext to cohomology via the dual perfect complex lemma and set up the induction on quasi-compact opens with the induction principle (proof lines 8522-8526).

Affine case: represent K by a module complex K^bullet and E by a finite complex of finite projective modules P^bullet via the affine comparison, the perfect-affine lemma and the More on Algebra definition; the tensor product is represented by the total complex of P^bullet tensor K^bullet; by induction on the length of P^bullet it suffices to show H^i(P^a tensor K^bullet) countable, which follows since P^a is a direct summand of a finite free module and H^i(K^bullet) is countable (proof lines 8529-8546).

Gluing: if U = V cup W and the result holds for V, W and V cap W, the Mayer-Vietoris sequence expresses H^i(U, K tensor E) through the countable groups on V, W, V cap W and quotients, so it is countable; with the affine case and the induction principle this finishes the lemma (proof lines 8549-8553).
proof_roadmap: Reduce Ext to cohomology and set up the induction principle (proof lines 8522-8526).
Prove the affine case by representing the tensor product as a total complex and counting via direct summands of finite free modules (proof lines 8529-8546).
Glue by Mayer-Vietoris over unions of quasi-compact opens (proof lines 8549-8553).
